games.title: Words to 1000
games.skillName: Numbers to 1000 in words, comparing and ordering
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to compare and order numbers up to 1000; read and write numbers up to 1000 in numerals and in words
games.instruction: Read it, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Look at the hundreds first, then the tens, then the ones.

questions.ask: What is 'three hundred and forty-two' in numerals?
What is 'six hundred and five' in numerals?
What is 'nine hundred and ninety' in numerals?
What is 'two hundred and twelve' in numerals?
In 784, what does the 7 stand for?
Which is the greatest: 458, 485, 548 or 584?
Which is the smallest: 709, 790, 907 or 970?
Which sign makes 640 ? 604 true?
Which list is in order, smallest first?
What is 'one thousand' in numerals?

games.title: Check It Twice
games.skillName: Estimating and checking with inverse operations
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to estimate the answer to a calculation and use inverse operations to check answers
games.instruction: Estimate or check, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Round each number first, or undo the sum with the opposite operation.

questions.ask: Estimate 198 + 403 by rounding each number to the nearest hundred.
Estimate 52 + 39 by rounding each number to the nearest ten.
Which is the best estimate for 299 + 101?
Estimate 487 − 212 by rounding each number to the nearest hundred.
Estimate 71 + 18 + 29 by rounding each number to the nearest ten.
312 + 145 = 457. Which calculation checks it?
640 − 230 = 410. Which calculation checks it?
Ben says 523 − 198 = 325. Which check shows he is right?
Kim works out 250 + 380 = 530. Checking with 530 − 380 shows...

games.title: Times Tower
games.skillName: Multiplying two-digit numbers by one-digit numbers
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to write and calculate mathematical statements for multiplication and division using the multiplication tables that they know, including for two-digit numbers times one-digit numbers, using mental and progressing to formal written methods
games.instruction: Work it out, then tap the answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Multiply the tens, then the ones, then add the two parts.

questions.ask: What is 23 × 3?
What is 14 × 5?
What is 32 × 4?
What is 25 × 4?
What is 12 × 6?
What is 41 × 3?
What is 18 × 2?
What is 13 × 8?
What is 27 × 3?
What is 15 × 4?

games.title: Fraction Mix Lab
games.skillName: Fractions of a set, adding, subtracting and ordering fractions
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to recognise, find and write fractions of a discrete set of objects: unit fractions and non-unit fractions with small denominators; add and subtract fractions with the same denominator within one whole [for example, 5/7 + 1/7 = 6/7]; compare and order unit fractions, and fractions with the same denominators
games.instruction: Read it, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Keep the bottom number the same, or share into equal groups first.

questions.ask: What is 1/4 of 20?
What is 2/3 of 12?
What is 3/5 of 10?
Which unit fraction is the biggest?
Which unit fraction is the smallest?
Which list is in order, smallest first?
Which fraction is the greatest?

games.title: Weigh and Pour
games.skillName: Adding and subtracting mass, capacity and length
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to measure, compare, add and subtract: lengths (m/cm/mm); mass (kg/g); volume/capacity (l/ml)
games.instruction: Work it out, then tap the answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Check both amounts use the same unit, then add or subtract.

questions.ask: How many grams are in 1 kg?
A jug holds 750 ml. You pour out 250 ml. How much is left?
A ribbon is 45 cm. Another is 38 cm. What is their total length?
Add 2 m 30 cm and 1 m 50 cm.
One bag is 5 kg. Another is 3 kg. How much heavier is the first bag?
Which is the heaviest?

games.title: Market Stall Change
games.skillName: Adding and subtracting money and giving change
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to add and subtract amounts of money to give change, using both £ and p in practical contexts
games.instruction: Work it out, then tap the right amount.
games.hint: Not quite. Change everything to pence, or count on from the price.

questions.ask: A book costs £3.45. You pay with £5. How much change?
A pen costs 85p and a ruler costs 60p. What is the total?
You pay £1 for a 37p lolly. How much change?
Juice costs 75p and crisps cost 50p. What is the total?
You pay £10 for a £6.40 toy. How much change?
How much is £3 + 45p?
You have £2. A comic costs £1.25. How much is left?
Two cakes cost 65p each. How much for both?

games.title: Calendar Countdown
games.skillName: Seconds, days in each month, years and leap years
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to know the number of seconds in a minute and the number of days in each month, year and leap year; compare durations of events [for example, to calculate the time taken by particular events or tasks]
games.instruction: Read it, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Try the knuckle trick for months, or count on in minutes.

questions.ask: How many seconds are in a minute?
How many days are in a year that is not a leap year?
How many days are in a leap year?
How many days does February have in a leap year?
How many days does February have in a year that is not a leap year?
How many days does April have?
Which month has 30 days?
A race took 75 seconds. How long is that?
Mia's bath took 20 minutes. Jo's took 35 minutes. How much longer was Jo's?
A film starts at 2:00 and ends at 3:30. How long is it?

games.title: Lines and Angles
games.skillName: Comparing angles with a right angle and naming lines
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to identify whether angles are greater than or less than a right angle; identify horizontal and vertical lines and pairs of perpendicular and parallel lines
games.instruction: Read it, then tap the right answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Picture a square corner, or picture the lines, then try again.

questions.ask: At 2 o'clock, how does the angle between the clock hands compare with a right angle?
At 4 o'clock, how does the angle between the clock hands compare with a right angle?
At 3 o'clock, how does the angle between the clock hands compare with a right angle?
At 6 o'clock, the hands make a straight line. How big is that angle?
At 5 o'clock, how does the angle between the clock hands compare with a right angle?
How does the corner of a square compare with a right angle?
A line going straight across, like the horizon, is...
A line going straight up and down, like a flagpole, is...
Lines that never meet and stay the same distance apart are...
Two straight lines that meet at a right angle are...
